title: Interpreting a statement of financial position
notes: Authored 2026-10-06 under standard v0.2.0-draft. All claims are provenance generated_gap, verification unverified.

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Interpret a simple statement of financial position: deduce how a business finances its activities and what it owns, and weigh selling inventories to raise finance.

blocks.heading: A snapshot on one date
blocks.text: A statement of financial position lists the assets a business owns, the liabilities it owes and the capital invested by its owners, at one point in time. It is a snapshot: it answers 'where does the business stand on this date?', whereas the income statement reports profit over a period, and profit is not the same as cash. Reading starts with the headings: non-current assets are the long-term resources the business works with; current assets and current liabilities show the short-term flow of goods, credit and cash; capital and liabilities together answer the financing question.

blocks.heading: Worked example: reading the finance mix
blocks.text:
On 31 December 2025 the statement of Ongwediva Hardware, a tool retailer, shows non-current assets of N$40 000; current assets of inventories N$12 500, trade receivables N$9 400 and cash N$3 200; capital N$45 100; a long-term loan of N$10 000; and current liabilities of trade payables N$8 000 and an overdraft N$2 000. Each side totals 65 100.

Deductions. Financing: capital supplies about 69 per cent of the funds, the loan about 15 per cent and short-term credit about 15 per cent, so the business is financed mainly from its owners' money. Assets: current assets of N$25 100 against N$10 000 of current liabilities leave a margin of N$15 100, suggesting near-term debts are covered; a lender is likely to read the small overdraft as modest borrowing.

blocks.heading: Selling inventories to raise finance
blocks.text: When a business is short of cash it can sell part of its inventories. Condition: it holds goods buyers want. Mechanism: the goods pass to buyers and their value arrives as cash - finance raised from inside the business rather than borrowed. Consequence: the cash can clear a pressing overdraft or supplier, easing the strain on the business. The costs run the same chain in reverse: goods sold in a hurry may go for less than their usual price, and lines sold off are lines no longer earning future revenue, so the relief is one-off.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: Topic 5.1 sets out the sources of finance the mix here is drawn from. Topic 5.2 treats working capital - current assets against current liabilities, the margin read above. Topic 5.3 explains the income statement this snapshot sits beside; Topic 5.5 turns both into ratios.
